newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks track Wall Street for modest fall.
newsitem.headline: French stocks track Wall Street for modest fall.

text.p: French stocks finished slightly lower on Monday after mirroring a second day of selling on Wall Street, brokers said.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 8.43 points, or 0.33 percent, at 2,566.13. The Dow index, whose 2.27 percent fall on Friday prompted an early selloff to as low as 2,528.30, was also down 0.33 percent when the French market closed.

The bourse drew some support from the dollar's strength. "At these levels, the dollar's positive for the bourse," one broker said. But investors were cautious ahead of U.S. consumer price data due on Tuesday. Volume was a modest 4.7 billion francs.

* Cie de Suez rose 1.88 percent to 286.60 francs after the resumption of trade on Monday following the formal announcement of its plan to merge with Lyonnaise des Eaux. The companies said Suez shareholders will be offered one share in Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux for 2.05 Suez shares. Suez, which had been under pressure from its shareholders to pay a special dividend, said it would triple the payout.

"People are happy with the deal," one trader said. Because of the dividend, buying Suez is a safe way to invest in the deal, he said. The rise also anticipates the parities. Lyonnaise shares closed up 0.19 percent at 541 francs.
* SGS-Thomson fell 4.28 percent to 376 francs after the semiconductor company reported a drop in first-quarter net income to $90.50 million from $175 million.

* Canal Plus extended a rise fuelled by its increased weighting in the CAC index, adding 1.88 percent to 1,137 francs. Canalsatellite forecast its digital channel collection would break even in 1998. Stakeholder Havas rose 1.43 percent to 412.30 francs.
* Accor rose 1.65 percent to 860 francs. Brokers say investors are endorsing the new chairman and the stock is well oriented technically. One said he suspected stake-building.
